newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares up at noon on domestic buying.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares up at noon on domestic buying.

text.p: Shanghai B shares were sharply up at midday on Monday mainly due to buying by domestic investors on the back of bullish sentiment, brokers said.
The B index surged 3.195 points or 3.39 percent to 97.326 points on volume of 14.481 million shares worth $9.59 million, compared with $10.103 million on Friday.

Follow-up buying from retail domestic investors was strong, but institutions are mixed over the trend going forward, so volume did not grow, brokers said. They said they expected a correction this afternoon.

"The strong A share performance sparked speculative buying by domestic investors," said one broker said. "But volume did not grow because investors are still worried that overheating on the market may spark a government crackdown."
"The index has risen too quickly over the past few weeks and a technical correction is unavoidable in the short term," another broker said.
Of 43 shares, 41 traded, with 33 up, seven flat and one down.
Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere Products was the star on institutional buying to support its new 100 million shares issue, surging $0.102 or 9.98 percent to $1.124 on volume of 510,200 shares.

Shanghai Narcisscus Electric Appliances Industry was the most actively traded on institutional cross-trading due to mixed views over its prospects, rising $0.004 or 2.04 percent to $0.200 on volume of 1.2 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index was sharply up on heavy speculative buying, but upward potential was limited due to increasing risks at such high levels, brokers said.
The index climbed 33.854 points or 2.21 percent to 1,567.969 points on volume of 552.9 million shares worth 8.0 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index rose 50.469 points or 1.18 percent to 4,330.083 points.
Beijing Tianqiao Department was the biggest winner on institutional buying, surging 0.89 yuan or 10.04 percent to 9.75 yuan on volume of 3.6 million shares.
